equity_bridge.item: Pension and postretirement benefit liability, after tax
equity_bridge.note: 825 at 2026-09-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet) x (1 - 23%); contributions are tax deductible

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: capacity growth plus yield, post-normalisation
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every trailing CAGR is measured off a pandemic base (FY2020 revenue 15,355, EPS -25.30, owner FCF negative; FY2022 EPS 2.23) and none is a usable forward rate. Equity CAGR (20.7-30.4%) diverges from revenue CAGR by far more than 30% and reflects balance-sheet repair, not compounding. The selected 3.5% is a judgment on mid-cycle capacity and yield growth.
historical_growth.notes: Annual FY2020-FY2025. Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award taxes; interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2022 1,158 (equity-award taxes not available), FY2023 -371, FY2024 3,667, FY2025 2,301. The series swings with aircraft delivery timing and working capital, so the 3-year CAGR is not informative. SBC plus equity-award taxes is ~0.4% of revenue, so owner and reported FCF growth do not diverge materially.

scenario_narratives.base: Fuel stays elevated through 2027, as management is planning for, then eases; fares already repriced in 2026 (revenue +15% on a +60% fuel price) hold most of their gain. Adjusted EBITDA margin recovers from ~9.4% in FY2026E to a 13.5% mid-cycle level by 2030, a little below the FY2023-25 average of 14.1% because more of the fleet is now rented through sale-leasebacks and airport rents are rising faster than revenue. That is roughly an 8% pretax margin: the long-stated double-digit target is not reached. United Next deliveries keep capex at 10-11% of revenue through 2030 before it glides to 6.5% as the order book completes in 2034, so owner FCF is slightly negative in 2027 and only reaches a ~5% margin in the terminal year. The NOLs and bonus depreciation shelter cash tax until about 2031.
scenario_narratives.bull: The fuel shock fades by 2028 while industry capacity discipline, weaker competitors (American, JetBlue, the ULCCs) and United's premium, MileagePlus/Chase co-brand, Starlink and Kinective Media revenue keep unit revenue up. Adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 16%, in line with FY2019 and consistent with a double-digit pretax margin. Capex is unchanged from base because the order book is contractual; the upside is all margin and a slightly faster top line, with the NOLs consumed sooner.
scenario_narratives.bear: No fuel hedge meets a demand downturn: jet fuel stays near 2026 levels while a recession cuts premium and corporate travel, so revenue falls in 2028 and fares cannot cover costs. Labour cost steps up further as the remaining work groups settle on the AFA pattern, Newark and O'Hare constraints cap growth at the best hubs, and mid-cycle adjusted EBITDA margin settles at 11%. Management defers deliveries, so capex falls faster than in base, but owner FCF is negative for the first three years against 26.4bn of gross debt, and almost all enterprise value goes to creditors. Equity value in this path is a thin residual; it is the leverage, not the operations, that drives the per-share result.

valuation_philosophy.summary: UAL is valued as a levered cyclical on mid-cycle owner free cash flow, not on peak or trough earnings. Three things dominate the value: the mid-cycle adjusted EBITDA margin (each point is worth roughly $17-20 per share), how long United Next keeps capex near 11% of revenue, and the 11.7bn of net debt plus pension that stands ahead of the equity. Special items, which include 931m of mostly sale-leaseback gains in 9M-2026, are excluded from the margin; the NOL shelter is modelled as a finite cash-tax ramp rather than a balance-sheet asset.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin: the 13.5% base sits between the 11% bear and 16% bull, and the equity value is highly geared to it
Jet fuel is unhedged; the 2026 shock took adjusted EBITDA margin from 13.4% to ~9.4%
Capex: 57bn of firm purchase commitments; delivery timing and the sale-leaseback mix move FCF by billions a year
FY0 revenue is an estimate resting on a secondary-sourced Q4 growth guide of 'above 20%'
The Analysis JSON's FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $9-$11 does not reconcile with the 10-Q figures (~$6-7 implied)
Terminal value is capped at 13x mid-cycle FCF; at 12x or 15x the base value moves roughly -$6 / +$12 per share
Operating lease liabilities of 7.9bn are excluded from net debt because rent is already inside EBITDA; adding them would double-charge

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 84.64-138.77
data_sources.financials: UAL 10-Q for Q3-2026 (balance sheet 2026-09-30, cash flow, EPS note, special charges note); 10-K FY2025 (share-based compensation, leases, firm commitments, NOL, capex outlook); UAL_Metrics.csv / core_metrics history
data_sources.qualitative: UAL_Analysis.json dated 2026-11-15 (guidance items there are partly secondary-sourced)

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q3-2026 10-Q EPS note (327.4m; basic 324.9m; 324.894m outstanding at 2026-10-15). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; anti-dilutive awards immaterial per the filing.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-09-30. SBC: FY2025 10-K share-based compensation plan cost table (148) less 9M-2025 stock-settled SBC (109) plus 9M-2026 stock-settled SBC (133), statements of stockholders' equity. Equity-award taxes: 'Stock issued for share-based awards, net of shares withheld for tax' FY2025 (108) less 9M-2025 (108) plus 9M-2026 (101). UAL publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed per the method rule; this is the conservative basis.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.4 gives cost of equity ~11.3%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.8% (10-K weighted rates 5.3-6.0%), ~4.5% after tax. At net-debt weights (~75% equity / 25% net debt) WACC is ~9.6%; at gross-debt weights (~58/42) ~8.4%. 9.0% used for all three scenarios: cyclicality, fuel exposure and leverage are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in per-scenario discount rates (adaptations (f), risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Under US GAAP (ASC 842) operating lease cost (aircraft rent, airport rent; FY2025 operating lease cost 894 plus 4,003 variable/short-term) is already an operating expense above operating income, so EBITDA as modelled is post-rent and lease_cost_pct_path is zero. Operating lease liabilities (934 current + 6,962 non-current at 2026-09-30) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases and sale-leaseback 'other financial liabilities' are inside the 26,398 debt figure and their amortisation is inside D&A. The growing use of aircraft sale-leasebacks shifts cost from capex to rent; the EBITDA margin paths are set net of that drift.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with the cyclical/lease adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'). An airline is an operating company whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; none of the non-FCF routes apply. FY0 is FY2026 ESTIMATED: 9M-2026 revenue 50,156 actual plus Q4 at +20% on Q4-2025's 15,397 (management guided 'above 20%', secondary-sourced) = ~68,630. FY0 is set to FY2026E rather than FY2025 because the 2026-09-30 balance sheet already contains nine months of FY2026 cash flow; projecting FY2026 as year 1 would count it twice. NET DEBT: debt, finance leases and other financial liabilities 1,848 current + 24,550 non-current = 26,398, less cash 6,648 and short-term investments 8,005 = 14,653 (the 'cash' input is cash plus short-term investments; restricted cash 146 excluded). INTEREST INCOME: not stripped from last_fcf because UAL is in net debt, not net cash; forward flows are built from EBITDA and so exclude both interest income (440 in 9M-2026) and interest expense, with the cash and the debt both in the bridge. last_fcf is therefore a levered TTM figure (TTM OCF 8,160 less TTM capex 7,044), depressed by the 740 flight-attendant ratification bonus paid September 2026. EBITDA BASIS: operating income plus D&A, EXCLUDING special items. 9M-2026 operating income of 3,539 includes 749 of net special credits (931 of gains, mostly aircraft sale-leaseback, less 182 ratification bonus); adjusted 9M operating income is 2,790 (5.6% margin) and adjusted EBITDA 5,085 (10.1%). FY2025 adjusted EBITDA 7,911 (13.4%), FY2024 8,136 (14.3%), FY2023 7,831 (14.6%), FY2019 ~15.8%. FY2026E ~9.4%. The core_metrics ebitda column is statutory and includes the gains. NOL: ~10.6bn of federal NOLs at 2025-12-31 (cash taxes 62 in FY2025 on 4,306 pretax) plus bonus depreciation on a ~7-8bn/yr capex programme are captured through the cash-tax ramp, NOT added to the bridge, so the shelter is counted once and expires. BUYBACKS: TTM repurchases 54 (27 in Q4-2025, 27 in 9M-2026; 637 in FY2025); the programme has effectively paused during the fuel shock, so the flat count is currently a modelling convention only partly funded. GUIDANCE DISCREPANCY: the Analysis JSON carries 'FY2026 adjusted EPS at the high end of $9-$11', secondary-sourced. It does not reconcile with the 10-Qs: 9M GAAP diluted EPS 7.74 less 662 of after-tax special credits (~2.02/share) is ~5.72 adjusted, and with the reported Q4 range of ~$0.50-$1.50 FY2026 adjusted EPS is ~$6-7. The model is built on the filings, not on the $9-$11 figure. TERMINAL: cap multiple 13x mid-cycle FCF (cyclical range 12-15x) binds in every scenario against a 15.8x Gordon value; it implies ~9x NOPAT and under 5x EBITDA, in line with where network carriers have traded.

base.capex_note: Firm purchase commitments at 2025-12-31: 5.6bn 2027, 7.4bn 2028, 9.0bn 2029, 8.7bn 2030, 13.8bn after, plus ~1.5-2bn/yr of non-aircraft capex, partly offset by sale-leaseback financing. Glides to 6.5% (1.4x D&A) by year 10 as United Next completes in 2034.
base.wc_capture_note: Advance ticket sales (10.7bn) and frequent-flyer deferred revenue (8.0bn) grow with revenue and exceed receivables and inventory; modest positive capture on the revenue change.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: UAL is unhedged against a fuel shock that is live now, carries 26.4bn of gross debt at BB+/Ba1, and its equity is a levered residual on a cyclical margin. Base 50%: management's own planning case is elevated fuel through 2027 with the double-digit pretax target not assured. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs fuel to normalise, fares to stick, and the industry to stay disciplined at the same time.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
